I can't prove this, because the statement is false whenever its hypotheses hold.

The hypothesis `e ∈ T.edgeSet` means `T` has at least one edge, so `V` has two distinct vertices `u ≠ v`. The conclusion requires `T1` and `T2` to be trees, so both are connected. In a connected graph, every vertex with some other vertex in `V` has a neighbour: take a walk from `u` to `v`, and its first edge shows `u ∈ T1.support`. The same argument applies to `T2`, so `u` lies in both supports. That contradicts `Disjoint T1.support T2.support`.

So no choice of `T1` and `T2` can satisfy the conclusion. The conclusion is unsatisfiable under the hypotheses, which means no proof exists. The intended statement was probably that the supports are not disjoint, or that the two components are vertex-disjoint as sets of vertices, which is a different claim. I left `/work/combi_brualdi_ch11_59.lean` unchanged, since the rules forbid altering the statement.

I give up.
